_doc: Approved target families per source technology. Versions are deliberately NOT pinned here (they go stale): stack-researcher pins exact versions at plan time from Context7 / official release pages and records them in the ADR. Edit 'preferred' to encode your org's standards.

version_policy.rule: Use the newest LTS (or newest stable if the project has no LTS) that has been released for at least 60 days and is inside its support window for >= 18 more months.
version_policy.evidence_required: Release date and end-of-support date with a source URL for every pinned component.

angularjs.notes: AngularJS is EOL. Angular keeps DI/templating mental model; React+TS for component rewrite. Strangler via angular-elements or route-by-route.

angular-legacy.notes: Use 'ng update' one major at a time; standalone components + signals at the end.

jquery.notes: Island-by-island replacement; keep server-rendered pages until each island is ported.

react-legacy.notes: Class components -> function+hooks; CRA -> Vite; enzyme -> Testing Library.

vue2.notes: Vue 2 is EOL; @vue/compat migration build first.

server-templates.notes: JSP/Razor/Thymeleaf/PHP views: decide SPA vs modern SSR in the ADR.

express-js.notes: Convert to TypeScript first, then framework.

java-spring-old.notes: javax -> jakarta namespace; OpenRewrite recipes for Boot 2->3.

dotnet-framework.notes: Use .NET Upgrade Assistant; WCF -> CoreWCF or gRPC/REST.

mysql.notes: Same-engine upgrade is lower risk; cross-engine only with a stated reason in the ADR.

sqlserver.notes: T-SQL procs are the main cross-engine cost.

oracle.notes: PL/SQL -> PL/pgSQL; use ora2pg for the assessment.
